files.purpose: Git.swift is the app's only wrapper around the git command line and the three forge CLIs (glab, gh, tea): every git process is spawned through Git.run with the argv prefix ["-c", "core.quotepath=false", "-c", "color.ui=false"], GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 over LoginEnvironment.current, a 120 s default budget and 300 s at named sites. It owns repository queries (status --porcelain=v2 parsing into GitStatus, branches into GitBranch, remote and forge detection), commit/publish (commitAll, push, pushBranch, createPullRequest, mergePullRequest with GitLab 405 retries), the Hydra landing primitives (captureTree over private GIT_INDEX_FILE indexes, commitWork, compare-and-swap updateRef, dirty/ignored/present path queries, hasOperationInProgress marker checks), checkpoint refs under refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/<thread>/<turn>-<phase> with WorkingTreeWatch-assisted tree capture, revert preview/restore, chunked diff, detached worktrees and three-way patch apply. At B3 (1.7.0) it gains a rebase-onto-remote capture (captureTree(paths:onto:from:)) that builds the team's paths on top of origin's current commit with per-file git merge-file, a force option on pushBranch for Hydra-owned branches, and a recovery path that turns a forge's 'already exists' failure into the URL of the existing request.

NEW createPullRequest fallback (:193-195): after the forge switch and before Self.check(result), `if !result.succeeded, let existing = Self.existingRequestURL(in: result, web: await remoteWebURL()) { return existing }`. A failed create whose output says the request already exists now returns that request's URL instead of throwing; the doc comment says a retried merge then carries on with that request rather than failing on it. remoteWebURL() is awaited on every failure (one extra git remote get-url origin) because it is an argument of the call.

NEW static existingRequestURL(in:web:) (:202-218), also called from AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:462: text = output + "\n" + errorOutput; nil unless text.lowercased() contains "already exist"; then the first #/https://\S+/# match that parses as a URL is returned (GitHub and Gitea print the address); otherwise the first #/!(\d+)/# match plus a non-nil web URL: when web.user is non-nil, URLComponents drops user and password (keeping the original when .url is nil), and the result is web.appending(path: "-/merge_requests/<digits>") (GitLab names it as !<number>). An unparseable https match falls through to the !<number> branch rather than returning nil.

NEW captureTree(paths:onto:from:) (:280-345): the team's paths rebuilt on top of `base` (origin/<target>, a descendant of `head`) so a checkout that fell behind does not open a merge request that conflicts on the forge (the doc comment records one finished job opening a conflicted merge request every five minutes). Scratch directory temporaryDirectory/droppy-code-rebase-<UUID> created with intermediates and removed in a defer; GIT_INDEX_FILE = scratch/index; read-tree <base> (checked, 120 s); upstream = set of `diff --name-only --no-renames -z <head> <base>` (renames count as delete+add); clean = paths not upstream-changed, added with add -A --ignore-errors --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul at 300 s when non-empty; contested paths resolved one by one; write-tree (checked); returns (tree, merged).

Contested-path table (:306-340), comparing byte contents: remote nil and working nil -> skip; remote present and working missing (team deleted) -> nil unless remote == ancestor, then rm --cached --quiet --ignore-unmatch -- <path> in the scratch index (checked); remote nil and working present (remote deleted) -> nil; both present and equal -> skip; both present and ancestor nil (added both sides differently) -> nil; otherwise working/ancestor/remote are written to scratch/current, common, other, `git merge-file --quiet -- current common other` runs with no GIT_INDEX_FILE at 120 s, any non-zero exit -> nil, the merged bytes are stored with hash-object -w --stdin (checked), mode = fileMode(base, path) ?? "100644", and update-index --add --cacheinfo "<mode>,<hash>,<path>" (checked) puts them into the scratch index; merged[path] = content for the caller to write into the checkout once the work has landed.

NEW private blobData(_:_:) (:347-351): cat-file blob <commit>:<path>, raw stdout bytes, nil on throw or non-zero exit. NEW private fileMode(_:_:) (:353-359): ls-tree -z <commit> -- <path>, first NUL record, first space-separated field, nil when absent.

CHANGED pushBranch(_:force:) (:387-392): new `force: Bool = false`; argv ["push", "-u"] + ["--force"] when force + ["origin", "refs/heads/<n>:refs/heads/<n>"], still 300 s. Doc: force is for a branch Droppy Code owns outright (a Hydra job's) which a retry rebuilds on a newer base, so its open merge request follows along instead of a second one being opened. B3 caller AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:348 passes force: ownBranch. With force false the argv is identical to B2.
Everything else (run/env prefix, status parsing, checkpoints, WorkingTreeWatch capture, indexPath cache, diff chunking, previewRestore/restore, apply) is byte-identical to B2 and only shifted.
unresolved_questions: captureTree(paths:onto:from:) mixes path bases: `diff --name-only` prints repository-root-relative names, `cat-file blob <rev>:<path>` is tree-root-relative, `ls-tree <rev> -- <path>` and the add/rm pathspecs are cwd-relative, and the working bytes are read from directory.appendingPathComponent(path). These agree only when the Git value's directory is the repository root; whether the B3 Hydra merge caller (AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:288) can run it from a subdirectory project is for the AppModel+HydraMerge reader to settle (compare upstream defect 84 / BLK-0004 for previewRestore).

The exact wording glab, gh and tea print when a request already exists is not in the pinned source; the port can only reproduce the source's substring test ("already exist", case-insensitive) and the !<number> / https:// extraction. Fixture texts for tests must be labelled as constructed, not observed.
